cards.front: Explain photosynthesis in your own words.
cards.back: Photosynthesis is the process plants, algae, and some bacteria use to convert light energy into chemical energy.
cards.evidence: The overall purpose is to store energy in glucose while releasing oxygen as a byproduct.
cards.reviewPrompt: Connect photosynthesis to energy and photosynthesis.

cards.front: Explain light-dependent reactions in your own words.
cards.back: The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts.
cards.evidence: Water molecules are split, oxygen is released, and energy carriers ATP and NADPH are produced.
cards.reviewPrompt: Connect light-dependent reactions to reactions and light-dependent.

cards.front: Explain calvin cycle in your own words.
cards.back: The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma of chloroplasts.
cards.evidence: It uses carbon dioxide, ATP, and NADPH to build sugar molecules.
cards.reviewPrompt: Connect calvin cycle to carbon and cycle.

cards.front: Explain cellular respiration in your own words.
cards.back: Cellular respiration is the process cells use to break down glucose and release usable energy as ATP.
cards.evidence: In aerobic respiration, oxygen is consumed and carbon dioxide and water are produced.
cards.reviewPrompt: Connect cellular respiration to respiration and glucose.

cards.front: Explain energy flow in your own words.
cards.back: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration form a cycle of matter and energy flow.
cards.evidence: Photosynthesis stores energy by building glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
cards.reviewPrompt: Connect energy flow to energy and cellular.

cards.front: Explain limiting factors in your own words.
cards.back: The rate of photosynthesis can be limited by light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature, and water availability.
cards.evidence: If one factor is too low or too high, the process slows even when other factors are favorable.
cards.reviewPrompt: Connect limiting factors to factors and limiting.
